lv-15Re.title: Sign: thick red border with thin white outline
lv-15Re.summary: Warning and speed signs have a thick red border with a thin white line around it. Each Baltic country has a slightly different border.

lv-6Wew.title: Sign: blue direction sign, stylised arrow
lv-6Wew.summary: Blue direction signs with white text. The arrowhead is more stylised than in Estonia and Lithuania, where the back of the arrowhead is vertical.

differs.how: Arrowhead has a vertical back edge
Arrowhead has a vertical back edge

lv-94iJ.title: House numbers: tall rectangles, many colours
lv-94iJ.summary: House numbers are often tall rectangles in several colours. This is uncommon in Estonia and Lithuania.

lv-BB6n.title: Google car: red Gen 4 car
lv-BB6n.summary: A red Gen 4 Google car appears here. It also exists in a few other European countries, including Lithuania, but not Estonia.

lv-CK38.title: Marker: blue km post parallel to road
lv-CK38.summary: All three Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker. Here it sits parallel to the road and has a number on one side only.

differs.how: Marker sits at a different angle to the road
Marker sits at a different angle to the road

lv-Ligx.title: Pole: hook insulators alternating left-right
lv-Ligx.summary: Pole tops with hook-shaped insulators that alternate left, right, left. Much rarer in the other two Baltic countries, but seen in some other European countries.

lv-PA6J.title: Landscape: wide open fields, little forest
lv-PA6J.summary: South of one town, the land is open with far more fields and much less forest than the rest of the country.

lv-RplU.title: Sign: bus stop sign with 5 bus windows
lv-RplU.summary: The bus on the bus stop sign has five windows. The other Baltic countries draw four.

lv-T9gT.title: Guardrail: white or red reflectors
lv-T9gT.summary: Normal A-type guardrails with white or red reflectors. Estonia has none, Lithuania uses orange.

lv-ZHtQ.title: Plate: long white, blue EU strip on left
lv-ZHtQ.summary: Long white plates with the standard blue European strip on the left.

lv-b4Ic.title: Houses: art nouveau old town
lv-b4Ic.summary: A historic city centre of grand art nouveau buildings, similar to Vienna in places. Unique in the whole Baltic region.

lv-eZ93.title: Google car: black Gen 4 car
lv-eZ93.summary: A black Gen 4 Google car appears here too. It is found in many European countries, including Lithuania, but not Estonia.

lv-k1bL.title: Houses: wood and white brick, steep metal roofs
lv-k1bL.summary: Wood and white brick houses with steep corrugated metal roofs. Newer ones may have pastel stone walls, and mixes of wood with white brick are common.

lv-lm-556772.title: Marker: electricity marker, black tip
lv-lm-556772.summary: Electricity markers with a distinctive shape: a black tip over a different colour below.

lv-lm-741987.title: Vehicles: white buses and trams, blue bottom
lv-lm-741987.summary: Buses and trams in the capital are white with a blue lower half, very similar to the Dutch ones.

lv-pjGP.title: Language: street is "iela"
lv-pjGP.summary: The word for street is iela, which exists only here. Rarely, in the capital, you may see "gatve" (gat.), the standard Lithuanian word.

lv-q1yp.title: Language: letters with bars and hooks
lv-q1yp.summary: Look for vowels with a bar on top (Ā Ē Ī) and consonants with a small hook (Ģ Ķ Ļ Ņ). Lithuanian is related; Estonian looks quite different.

differs.how: Related language but lacks these exact letters
Not a Baltic language, looks very different

lv-uPlz.title: Bollard: thin, slightly curved, numbered
lv-uPlz.summary: Thin, slightly curved bollard with a rectangular reflector on the front and two round ones on the back, white or orange. Black strip is slightly angled, often with numbers below.

differs.how: Estonian bollards have a different shape
Lithuanian bollards have a different shape

lv-xps4.title: Sign: pedestrian sign, 5 stripes, long legs
lv-xps4.summary: The pedestrian sign has five stripes and a figure with noticeably long legs. The other two Baltic countries show three stripes.

lv-xypN.title: Chevron: white with red arrow
lv-xypN.summary: White chevrons with red arrows. Many European countries use these, including Lithuania and Poland. Estonia, Russia and Ukraine reverse it: red with white arrows.
